issues.description: Register usage contradiction: the problem statement explicitly instructs that the pixel value loaded from the computed memory address should be placed into ECX (instruction: mov ecx, [esi]) so that printf is called with (EAX:x, EBX:y, ECX:value). The template's printing code (push ecx; push ebx; push eax; push message; call printf) also expects ECX to contain the pixel value. The solution implementation instead does mov eax, [esi] (loads the pixel into EAX) before restoring saved registers with pop ebx / pop eax, which overwrites the loaded value. As a result, the value passed to printf is incorrect and the solution violates the exercise's explicit register contract, which will confuse students about the expected register usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution conform to the problem's register contract: load the pixel into ECX (use mov ecx, [esi]) at a point where it will not be overwritten by subsequent pops, or move the mov into ECX to after the pops that restore saved registers. Concretely, replace mov eax, [esi] with mov ecx, [esi], or perform mov ecx, [esi] after the pop ebx / pop eax sequence so the value in ECX remains intact when printf is called.
